findings.claim: The change adds a new runtime dependency (`tzdata`, unpinned) to `addons/cloud-sync/backend/requirements.txt`, a file the touch-point list does not name, and the spec it implements says the change adds no new dependency.
findings.impact: Every backend image build now installs an extra, unpinned package from PyPI (backend/Dockerfile:21-23 pip-installs every addon requirements.txt). Its version moves with each rebuild. Zone acceptance (`is_valid_timezone`, which the I2/I6/I9 behaviour relies on, including the `Asia/Calcutta` alias the tests expect) now depends on that package instead of the image's system tzdata. Nobody planned or reviewed this as a build-surface change.
findings.evidence: addons/cloud-sync/backend/requirements.txt: `+# Keeps legacy zone names (Asia/Calcutta) that browsers report and slim tzdata drops.` `+tzdata`. backend/Dockerfile:21-23 installs it into the backend image. The spec's item 10 says: 'No new dependency: `zoneinfo` and `croniter` are already available in the backend image'. The touch-point list names backend/schemas.py, service.py and router.py, and does not name requirements.txt.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is broken. This is a path outside the declared touch points that also contradicts the spec's non-functional item 10, so the plan needs to be revised to name it (and to decide whether to pin it).

findings.proposed_fix: Add `backend/requirements.txt` (tzdata) to the touch points and correct the spec's 'No new dependency' line, or drop the package if the system zoneinfo is enough. Consider pinning a version range, as croniter is pinned.

findings.claim: The PUT body validation was put in a new module, `addons/cloud-sync/backend/settings.py`, which the touch-point list does not name; the list places that validation in `backend/schemas.py`.
findings.impact: The load-time rules now exist twice: once in the `SyncConfig`/`SyncMapping` validators (schemas.py) and once in settings.py (`_check_row`, `_check_cross_rows`, `_check_schedule`, and so on). If a later rule change touches only one copy, PUT and load disagree. A body that settings.py accepts but `SyncConfig` rejects raises inside `checked.to_config()` (service.py save_config) and answers 500 instead of the 422 `{errors}` shape. The file is still not written in that case, so I3's 'unchanged file' part holds, but its '422 in the {errors} shape' part would not.
findings.evidence: New file addons/cloud-sync/backend/settings.py (208 lines: `check_body`, `BodyCheck.to_config`). It is imported in service.py as `from .settings import ConfigError, check_body`. The touch-point list says: '`backend/schemas.py`: ... the PUT body validation that collects every error'.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant is broken today: both copies of the rules currently agree, as far as I read them. This is a path outside the declared touch points, and it carries a drift risk.

findings.claim: Three new frontend modules sit outside the settings-section component and are not the listed `api.ts`: `frontend/settingsApi.ts` (the GET/PUT /config client), `frontend/settingsDraft.ts` (remote split/join, zone choice) and `frontend/scheduleForm.ts` (cron/preset round trip).

The touch-point list names `api.ts` for the API client and a Container/Presenter component for the section. A reviewer who follows that list would look for the /config client and the round-trip logic in the wrong files.
findings.evidence: New files in the diff: addons/cloud-sync/frontend/settingsApi.ts, settingsDraft.ts and scheduleForm.ts. `api.ts` changes only `SyncStatusResponse.timezone`.
